hook.line: Your sign to ask ChatGPT what they look like
hook.visual: Phone screen recording of the ChatGPT app in dark mode, keyboard up, with a red two-line title at the top; the user types 'Hey' and the bot answers with emojis.

beats.what: Red title text over the ChatGPT app; user sends 'Hey'.
ChatGPT replies 'what do u want' with emojis, a playful personality beat.
Long pasted prompt appears asking for a casual, failed iPhone selfie of itself.
Image generation starts: the dotted placeholder shows 'Making the first draft'.
Second red title says the full prompt is in the caption, while the progress dots build.
Status changes through 'Finishing up' and 'Adding final touches' as the dot pattern fills.
Reveal: a blurry, badly lit selfie of a young woman appears as 'ChatGPT's' face.
Keyboard returns as she starts typing a reply, then the video ends.

why_it_works: Built-in suspense: about 13 s of 'making the first draft' progress dots make viewers wait for the face reveal.
'Your sign to' framing is a direct invitation to try it, so comments fill with people's own results (12k comments).
Prompt hidden in the caption pushes viewers to open the caption and save the video for later.
weaknesses: No voice and no face, so nothing distinguishes the creator; anyone could post the same recording.
Most of the runtime is a loading animation with small UI text (median text height 2.6% of frame).
The payoff only appears at 22 s, so viewers who scroll early never see it.
for_robert: Steal the progress-bar suspense: let Fred wait impatiently beside a generating image and react at the reveal, but compress the wait to a few seconds instead of 13.
